fix(collector): the sweep sends a retiring session its retire again until one is answered, and every hand-in settles (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.0iu)

A retire whose turn threw left the record retiring with nothing to send
it again, so it stayed counted and the sweep never disarmed. The sweep
now sends every retiring record its retire again. An answer removes the
record only while it is still in the retiring period that send belongs
to, so an answer that arrives late cannot remove a record that was
revived or retired again. The record stays until then, because the
renderer may still hold the session's document, and a new record at
seq 1 would be refused.

Every hand-in goes through one path that logs a rejected delivery,
meaning the host's own recording of the turn threw, at error with the
session. Before this, a rejection reached the process's
unhandledRejection handler, which shuts the daemon down. That fixes the
world-state hand-in as well as the retire.

test(frame-feed): the unseen-pane case waits for its server's answer and spans its draws on the daemon's clock (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.5qt) (#714)

* test(frame-feed): the unseen-pane case waits for its server's answer and spans its draws on the daemon's clock (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.5qt)

The case slept 1.5 s betting the stub tmux server had answered, then
counted draws in a 2 s real window. Until the answer lands the pane
counts as shown and draws at the moving rate, so a slow spawn under the
full worker tier overran the count. It now waits for the daemon's
visibility line, then measures three draws on the daemon's monotonic
clock and asserts they span at least a still period: load only lengthens
that span. Forcing every pane shown fails it (106 ms).

* test(frame-feed): the unseen-pane case pins its bar moving, waits through the stream's own wait, and bounds three draws by two still periods (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.5qt)

Review pass (high): the visibility wait runs through waitFor, so the
stream's end is part of it and it gets the draw wait's budget; the span
uses elapsedMs; the bound is the two still periods the comment argues
for; and the closing summary's unseen count shows the bar was moving.
Forcing every pane shown fails it (104 ms against 1998).

* test(frame-feed): the unseen-pane case fits its waits inside the case's timeout, names the server's lines when it fails, and bounds its slack by the moving period (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.5qt)

Review pass (medium): both waits take 10 s, so a stall fails by name
before jest's 30 s; the visibility wait's failure lists that server's
lines; and the span's slack is a moving period rather than a copied
timer resolution, so it cannot drift from the feed's constants.
